 Judgment
Not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation, petitioner has come up with this appeal under Section 173(1) of the M.V.Act seeking enhancement.
2. For the sake of convenience the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioner that on 22.04.2015, at about 7.00 a.m, in order to attend nature's call, he was proceeding towards Managuli Bypass Ring Road, near Chidambara Temple.

At that time a tanker lorry bearing registration No.KA-02/AB- 3310 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle'), came in a rash or negligent manner and after the driver lost control over the vehicle, it dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact petitioner sustained several grievous injuries and despite prolonged treatment including surgery, he is not completely cured.
He is suffering from permanent partial disability affecting his earning capacity.
As the owner and insurer respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation and hence the petition.

4. Respondent No.2 appeared and filed written statement disputing the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, the accident, nature of the injuries sustained and that it has resulted in permanent partial disability.
It has also disputed that the vehicle was covered by a valid policy and that driver was holding a valid driving license and sought for dismissal of the petition against it.
5. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
6. Petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and the Doctor as PW-2.

He has relied upon Ex-P1 to 13.
7.
Respondent No.2 has not led any evidence on its behalf.

However, copy of the insurance policy is marked with consent as Ex.R1.
8.
Vide the impugned judgment and award
the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition granting compensation in a sum of Rs.3,76,226/- and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same with interest at 9% p.a.

The details of compensation granted are as under:

 Pain and sufferings 40,000/-

9.
During the course of arguments, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Tribunal has erred in restricting the percentage of disability at 10%.
The compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.
No compensation is granted towards loss of amenities of life and also loss of income during laid up period.
10. On the other hand the learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and sought for dismiss of the appeal.

11. Heard arguments of both sides and perused the record.
12.

Having regard to the fact that respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle and that at the time of accident, it was covered by a valid policy issued by respondent No.2 has attained finality.
13. Now the only question that is required to be decided whether the compensation granted is just and reasonable or it calls for any enhancement.
Though the petitioner has claimed that he was aged 55 years at the time of accident, based on records the Tribunal has rightly considered his age as 58 years and appropriate multiplier 9.

In the absence of proof of exact income, based on minimum wages and having regard to the fact that the accident is of the year 2015 the Tribunal has correctly taken the income of the petitioner as Rs.8,000/- p.m.
14.
PW-2 Orthopedic Surgeon has deposed that petitioner has suffered 33% of limitation of movements of the particular limb.
As admitted by him, he has not calculated the whole body disability.
Therefore, the Tribunal is justified in reducing the disability to 10% of the whole body.

However, while calculating the loss of future earnings, the Tribunal has not added loss of future prospects, as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram And Others1 (Magma Insurance Company case).

sentences.text: Since the petitioner is coming under the age group of 51-60, 10% of his earning is required to be added.
10% of Rs.8,000/- comes to Rs.800/-.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner is required to be taken at Rs.8,800/-p.m.
With these components, the loss of future earnings is Rs.8,800 x 12 x 9 x 10% = Rs.95,040/- as against Rs.86,400/- granted by the Tribunal.
15. The Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head laid up period.
Having (2018) 18 SCC 130 regard to the fact that petitioner has suffered fracture of lateral malleolous, fracture of 5th metacarpal neck, fracture of 2nd to 8th ribs on the right side.

3 regard to the age of petitioner, it would be reasonable to expect him to be under treatment for three months.

sentences.text: At the rate of Rs.8,000/- p.m, petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.24,000/- under the head loss of earnings during laid up period.
16. The Tribunal has also not granted any compensation under the head loss of amenities of life.

Taking into consideration the nature of the injuries suffered, period of treatment, it would be appropriate and reasonable to grant compensation in a sum of Rs.30,000 /- under the head loss of amenities of life.

17. The Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.10,000/- under the head conveyance,
food and nourishment.
Looking to the nature of the injuries suffered and period of treatment, it would be appropriate to enhance the same to Rs.15,000/-.
So far as the compensation granted under the other heads are concerned, they are just and reasonable and does not call for interference.

18. Thus, in all petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.4,43,866/- as against Rs.3,76,226/- granted by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation.
